newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade on Tuesday, with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. June leading indicators data, which is forecast to show a gain of 0.1 percent compared with a 0.3 percent increase reported in May, dealers said.

"Rates were quietly steady in the morning except for some light activity at the long end of the market. Some traders were waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the (U.S. June) leading indicators," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact as the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions for the day," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday, Wednesday/Thursday and week-fixed were unchanged from Monday's common 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, respectively.
Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, six-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 and nine-months unchanged at 5-7/8 5-3/4 percent.
Twelve-months rose 1/16 percentage point to 6 5-7/8 percent. - P.Theseira (65-870-3085)
